name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,588

clue.text: Music producer Parisian thugs attacked

indicators.note: something attacked is knocked about and left in disarray, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: all thirteen letters of the two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A gang of Paris heavies sets upon a record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' reads as a person in the studio, but it means an instrument that produces music.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitar is an instrument, and an instrument is literally a thing that makes musical sound.

clue.text: Big cheese Diana Ross once cut to get slice of Ossau-Iraty

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so the final letter of the singer's group name is dropped
a slice is a small piece, here just the opening letter of the cheese name

blocks.note: Diana Ross was lead singer of the Supremes, so she was once a Supreme
the first letter of the French sheep's cheese

explanation.surface: A Motown star trims a wedge from a Basque sheep's cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossau-Iraty is a sheep's-milk cheese from the French Pyrenees, chosen to echo 'Big cheese'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms for the person in charge, the boss at the top of an organisation.

clue.text: Info gathered by heartless adjunct for spy

indicators.note: without a heart, a word keeps only its outside letters and loses everything between
something gathered by another is taken in and held inside it

blocks.note: just the first and last letters of the word
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An assistant without scruples collects intelligence on behalf of a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is an operative who works covertly gathering intelligence, the same role as a spy.

clue.text: Country lad, nice in an odd sort of way

indicators.text: in an odd sort of way
indicators.note: doing something in an odd way means arranging it unusually, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rural boy who is pleasant, though somewhat eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country lad' reads as a farm boy; 'Country' is really the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a Nordic island nation in the North Atlantic, so it is a country.

clue.text: Very powerful gig by drug-addled singer?

blocks.note: first meaning: built for great speed or output, as with an engine
second meaning, read cryptically: a stoned musician's show is literally a concert given while intoxicated

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading: 'high' as intoxicated, and a gig as a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes machines or cars with exceptional power and speed, so it fits a strong engine.

clue.text: Old city man is earnest and persistent

blocks.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A man from an ancient town is described as serious and dogged.
explanation.definitionFit: An urgent plea or request is pressing and insistent, made seriously and repeated until it is answered.

clue.text: Teetotal locum associated with English judge

blocks.note: a locum is a stand-in worker, a temp
to judge something is to rate it

explanation.surface: A sober stand-in doctor teams up with an English judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A locum is a doctor or priest covering for someone temporarily.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate originally means moderate, and in the temperance movement sense it describes someone abstaining from alcohol.

clue.text: Scottish squad of soldiers?

blocks.note: first meaning: the Glasgow football club
second meaning: elite troops, such as the US Army's light infantry

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a single Scottish army unit; the two halves are separate senses. Rangers is a major Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club is named after its players, and the word also names specialist infantry trained for raids.

clue.text: Primate touring southern part of church

indicators.note: touring means going all the way round, so one word circles the other

explanation.surface: A monkey goes sightseeing in the south of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' could be an archbishop, which suits the church setting, but here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church building, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Appointment in Battle

blocks.note: first meaning: a booked meeting or commitment
second meaning: a military clash between forces

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a posting during a war; 'in' only joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an arranged commitment to meet and a fight between armies in combat.

clue.text: Woman in bed with touch of arthritis

indicators.note: only a touch means the smallest amount, here a single opening letter

blocks.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train

explanation.surface: A woman confined to bed with a little joint pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a female given name, and crosswords often define names simply by the person's sex.

clue.text: Rubbish German article about the Queen's fancy man

blocks.note: to pan a show is to rubbish it in a review
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Slating a German newspaper story about the monarch's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy man' suggests a lover but is used here loosely for a pimp, one who procures for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A panderer is a pimp, someone who procures sex for others, and a fancy man is old slang for a pimp.

clue.text: Officer that's potty about men

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

blocks.note: a commode is a chair with a chamber pot

explanation.surface: An officer who is crazy about the men under him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like an adjective meaning mad, but it is the noun, a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A commodore is a naval officer ranking above captain and below rear admiral.

clue.text: Man and midges involved in psychological warfare?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up and complicated, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A man locked in a battle of nerves with biting insects.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means manipulative tactics used to unsettle an opponent mentally, which the question mark marks as loose.

clue.text: In this country you might hear an insect

indicators.note: hearing points to how something is said rather than how it is written

blocks.note: the name of the Southeast Asian nation, said one common way, matches a parasitic bug

explanation.surface: A claim that in some land you may catch the sound of a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked nation in Southeast Asia, bordering Vietnam and Thailand.

clue.text: Function of wickedness? Evil primarily!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about what purpose wickedness serves, answered by evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' reads as purpose, but it is the trigonometric sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine is a trigonometric function, giving the ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse.

clue.text: Medics turned up around river to get washed

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means flipped to read from bottom to top
around means encircling, so one word is put inside the other

blocks.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Doctors arrive at a river to clean up.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to scrub clean vigorously, so scoured describes something thoroughly cleaned.

clue.text: Give up the ales or rum?

indicators.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar, so the letters come out strangely arranged

explanation.surface: Should one abandon beer, or switch to spirits?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink offered as an alternative to ale, but it is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is to become discouraged and stop trying, the idiomatic sense of giving up.

clue.text: European permit that covers chaps in a group

indicators.note: covering something means enclosing it, so one word wraps the other

explanation.surface: A European licence that applies to a bunch of men.
explanation.definitionFit: An element can be a distinct section of a population, as in a rowdy element in the crowd.

clue.text: Embarrassed cuddling Jade in bed?

indicators.note: cuddling means holding close in an embrace, so one word is wrapped round another

blocks.note: to jade is to weary, to tire

explanation.surface: Someone blushes at hugging a woman called Jade in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jade' looks like a woman's name but is the verb to wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: Having retired for the night means having gone to sleep, which the question mark signals as an indirect description.

clue.text: Note produced by opera singer on radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a high male voice in opera

explanation.surface: A musical note sung by an opera star during a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music, but it is a banknote; a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound banknote is called a tenner in everyday British speech, so it is a kind of note.

clue.text: Lengthy word? Interminable, perhaps?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a long word could be described as endless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminable' is itself a lengthy word, which is the joke; 'perhaps' marks the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lasts for an extended time, seemingly without end, could loosely be called interminable.

clue.text: Large housing project in European country

explanation.surface: A big residential development somewhere in a European nation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a housing estate is a large planned development of homes, often built by a council.

clue.text: Run into one who is trying to sell fish

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside

blocks.clueFragment: one who is trying to sell
blocks.note: a tout pushes tickets or goods on people

explanation.surface: Bumping into a salesman hawking fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout is a freshwater fish related to salmon, widely caught for food and sport.

clue.text: Bulge of porcine men needing to get in shape!

indicators.note: being put into shape means being reformed, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: The paunch of piggish men who ought to get fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominence is a part that projects outward, such as a hump or swelling, so it is a protrusion.

clue.text: Awful sort of revolutionary shot by soldiers

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for shot runs backwards

blocks.note: a shot is a go, an attempt
Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A dreadful kind of rebel executed by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a rebel but simply signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a cruel, frightening person, from the man-eating giant of folk tales.

clue.text: Desert an idiot travels about, being lost

indicators.note: travelling about means wandering here and there, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: A fool wanders across the desert and loses his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a verb meaning abandon, but it is just part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorientated means confused about direction or location, the state of someone who has lost their bearings.
